title: Fictional Maritime Exercise Reporting — Illustrative Dossier
dek: A made-up example demonstrating how IPR might distinguish official statements and editorial comparisons.
research_question: How do two imaginary ministry releases characterize different training objectives without treating those statements as independently verified operational outcomes?

scope.included: Two invented official exercise announcements with distinct reporting dates.
scope.excluded: No real events, performance measures, historical completeness, or public-source use.
scope.method: Fixture only: hypothetical source claims compared without asserting operational facts.
scope.collection_limits: Completely synthetic. This is not a collected archive or real-world evidentiary basis.

overview: In this wholly invented example, two fictional ministries described exercise participation using different editorial emphases. This sentence is not a factual IPR finding.

sections.heading: Reported training objectives
sections.intro: Attributed descriptions below are fictional assertions by imagined publishers.

claims.text: The hypothetical Alpha ministry described communications drills as a training objective.

event_period.date_basis: Fictional Alpha release dated 2026-08-12 is depicted as announcing a planned activity; not a real-world event.

claims.limits: A ministry assertion would not independently establish that the drill was conducted.

claims.text: The hypothetical Beta ministry characterized maritime safety as a stated objective.
claims.limits: The scope and implementation would remain unverified.

sections.heading: Differences in published framing
sections.intro: Compare issuing accounts without inferring the governments had conflicting intent.

claims.text: The two invented reports emphasize different training topics; this alone does not establish policy disagreement.
claims.limits: Different exercise types, genres, dates or contexts could explain the wording.
